verdict.rationale: Jitsu's pipeline runs unattended once configured. Functions automatically filter, transform and enrich every event, can call third-party services via the Fetch API, and webhook destinations can push events to Slack or other HTTP services. Connector syncs run as Kubernetes CronJobs, a reprocessing worker replays dead-lettered events, Kafka buffers data during warehouse downtime, and failure/recovery alerts arrive by email or Slack. Agents can also configure all of this through MCP, including headless API-key auth for CI. However, this is event-pipeline automation rather than a general-purpose background automation or workflow builder. Missing for 10: a general trigger/action automation builder, documented user-facing schedule configuration for syncs, autonomous agent-run background tasks, and independent hands-on corroboration.
